issues.description: Class Bitmap24: in the template header (example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp) the methods resize_buffer, save and set are declared under the 'protected:' section (lines 42-58), making them inaccessible to external code. In the solution header the same methods are declared public (lines 42-57). example_program/src/main.cpp (template) calls bitmap.resize_buffer(...) and bitmap.set(... ) (lines 36-44). Because the template header marks these member functions protected, those calls would be illegal and cause compilation errors for the provided template. This is a visibility mismatch between the template and solution that prevents the example program from compiling as-is.
issues.suggestedFix: Expose the Bitmap24 methods used from main (resize_buffer, save, set) as public in the template header to match the solution. Concretely, remove or move the 'protected:' label so these three declarations are under the public section (or explicitly mark them 'public:'). Ensure the template header's visibility for these members matches the solution to allow example_program/main.cpp to compile and run.
